newsitem.title: USA: Wickes to market KeySpan natgas.
newsitem.headline: Wickes to market KeySpan natgas.

text.p: KeySpan Energy Services said Thursday it will market natural gas at Wickes Lumber Co. home centers Northeast.

The agreement with Wickes Inc is believed to be the first of its kind between a building-materials supplier and a utility subsidiary, Brooklyn Union Gas Co in KeySpan's case, since gas-industry deregulation began last year, it said.

Wickes will have a dedicated sales force with expertise in energy services to offer natural-gas contracts at competitive rates to commercial and industrial property owners, builders of new residential communities, and homeowners.
KeySpan said it and Wickes will provide natural-gas and related energy services at market prices. The companies will also offer electricity when it becomes deregulated.
In addition to the energy commodities, the marketing venture will provide options on energy services provided by other KeySpan companies, spokesman Robert Mahony said.

He said some of these will be provided by the venture KeySpan energy management recently announced with Metricom Inc, a wireless Internet-services provider, to link advanced Internet service with energy products and services in 16 states in the Northeast and surrounding regions.

The wireless Internet services will support a variety of consumer services including medical alert, home security, remote meter reading, and appliance remote control, as well as wireless, mobile access to the Internet.

"Wickes, with its construction-market expertise and access to customers through 23 building centers in seven northeastern states, will enhance our ability to expand our market share," said Randy Magnani, KeySpan's chief operating officer.
The building centers involved in the agreement are in Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania.

For Wickes, this is a pilot project, said spokesman Robert Sherlock. The company's Wickes Lumber division is one of the largest suppliers of building materials in the United States with building centers in 24 states in the Midwest, Northeast, and South. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
